documentation_gaps.description: The diagnosis of type 2 diabetes is documented, but the presence of ketosis and metabolic acidosis (pH 7.30, HCO3 16, ketones positive) suggests possible diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) or ketosis-prone diabetes, which requires specification of the type of diabetes and the acute complication.
documentation_gaps.why_it_matters: Coding requires specificity for diabetes with ketoacidosis, which is a distinct condition from type 2 diabetes without complications. The documentation must clarify whether this is type 2 diabetes with ketoacidosis or another type.

specialist_trace.rationale: The documentation must specify whether this is type 2 diabetes with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) or a ketosis-prone phenotype, explicitly linking the pH 7.30, HCO3 16, and positive ketones to an acute metabolic decompensation. Please clarify the clinical severity of the acidosis (mild, moderate, or severe) and state the clinical significance of the hyperglycemia and ketosis in relation to the diabetes diagnosis, as the current label of “type 2 diabetes” alone is insufficient for accurate coding.
